findings.observation: Examined grading plans (Sheets 21, 22) using vision tool and found FFE values displayed on proposed building: 543.00, 545.00, 548.00, 552.00, and 553.00. Labels appear as "[FFE XXX.XX]" without any datum designation. Building Information table on Sheet 16 shows "FINISHED FLOOR ELEVATION: 553/548/543" also without datum. Reviewed Sheet 5 (General Notes) - no general statement about elevation datum. Sheet 53 (Topographic Survey) Survey Control note states "ELEVATIONS (NAVD88)" but this is a separate survey document. Sheet 28 pond calculations use "ft msl" notation in tables. No general note on civil sheets stating "all elevations shown are in MSL" or equivalent.
findings.reasoning: LDC 25-12-53(D)(1) requires lowest finished floor elevations to be shown in MSL datum. The FFE values are physically present on the grading plans and building information table, satisfying part of the requirement. However, the checklist deficiency specifically calls out "not shown...in MSL". The FFE labels lack explicit datum designation. While NAVD88 is referenced on Sheet 53 and is technically a mean sea level datum, there is no explicit connection made between the FFE values and this datum on the civil construction sheets where the FFEs appear. Best practice requires either labeling FFEs as "FFE XXX.XX MSL" or providing a general note that all elevations are in MSL/NAVD88.
findings.explanation: FFE values shown (543, 545, 548, 552, 553) but not explicitly designated as MSL datum on grading plans or building table.
findings.resolution: Add "MSL" or "(NAVD88)" designation to all FFE labels on grading plans and building information table, OR add a general note to Sheet 5 or grading plan sheets stating "All elevations shown are in feet, Mean Sea Level (NAVD88)".
